newsitem.title: UK: London coffee futures up $125 at $2,180 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: London coffee futures up $125 at $2,180 a tonne.

text.p: LIFFE's benchmark July coffee futures contract shot to $2,180 per tonne, up $125 from the previous close, within 20 minutes of its 0845 GMT opening on Monday.
Coffee is on its longest unbroken rally for two decades.
London robusta coffee futures had already shot up to a 15-1/2 month high on Friday in a new rally fired by a wave of fund and technical-related buying.

In New York, however, prices for the higher-quality arabica coffee futures pulled back later that day, pressured by speculative profit-taking and sentiment that the rally may have gone too far. Last week saw New York spot May futures trade at $2.79 per pound, the highest since June 1977.
A volatile mix of factors -- low stocks, tight supply from Colombia and fears that Brazil may have another frost -- has lured speculators to the futures markets.

Analysts said coffee-producing nations meeting in London this week may suspend export quotas to try to cool the explosive rally. As roasters in the U.S. and Europe pass on soaring world prices at the shops, some of the 14 members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) worry that people will switch to tea or soft drinks instead.
